title.value: Greenhouse gases emissions: estimating corporate non-reported emissions using interpretable machine learning
title.justification: The title is stated clearly in the paper and reflects the core focus of the study, which is estimating corporate greenhouse gas emissions using machine learning.
title.quote: Greenhouse gases emissions: estimating corporate non-reported emissions using interpretable machine learning

extractions.description: This paper proposes a machine learning-based model to estimate scope 1 and scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions for companies that have not reported their emissions. The model is designed to be interpretable and compares favorably with existing methodologies, yielding more accurate results. It includes a detailed methodological approach and validation against known datasets to ensure its accuracy and robustness.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The central theme of the paper is estimating greenhouse gas emissions, which directly relates to sustainable development through environmental accountability and emissions reduction strategies.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: GHG emissions reporting and auditing are not yet compulsory for all companies... We propose a machine learning-based model to estimate scope 1 and scope 2 GHG emissions of companies not reporting them yet.

primary_category.justification: The paper primarily addresses the measurement and estimation of greenhouse gas emissions, which is a crucial part of efforts to mitigate climate change impacts.
primary_category.quote: Our model, specifically designed to be transparent and completely adapted to this use case, is able to estimate emissions for a large universe of companies.

secondary_categories.justification: The paper involves the creation of a model that aids in understanding and estimating greenhouse gas emissions, contributing to climate science by providing tools to estimate environmental impacts.
secondary_categories.quote: We propose a machine learning-based model to estimate scope 1 and scope 2 GHG emissions of companies not reporting them yet.

secondary_categories.justification: It discusses the financial implications of reporting and correctly estimating GHG emissions for businesses, which ties into sustainable finance as companies need to manage and disclose climate-related financial risks and opportunities.
secondary_categories.quote: Overall GHG emissions assessments measure exposure to transition risk and negative cash flows coming from fines or outflows to competitors with greener footprints. They are useful for financial fundamental analysis and slowly implemented in corporate valuation methodologies.

primary_sub_category.justification: The paper's primary focus is on estimating and tracking greenhouse gas emissions using machine learning, fitting this sub-category.
primary_sub_category.quote: We propose a machine learning-based model to estimate scope 1 and scope 2 GHG emissions of companies not reporting them yet.

secondary_sub_categories.value: Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) and Disclosures
secondary_sub_categories.justification: The paper contributes to ESG by suggesting models for emission estimation that can be used in disclosure processes to meet regulatory requirements and engage stakeholders.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: Companies will need to report audited GHG emissions as well as a quantitative pathway and remediation plan to cancel their net emissions.

applications.justification: The paper directly focuses on creating a model for this application, providing a method to fill in data gaps in corporate emissions reporting.
applications.quote: We propose a machine learning-based model to estimate scope 1 and scope 2 GHG emissions of companies not reporting them yet.

applications.value: Improving accuracy of corporate GHG emissions data used in financial valuation and climate risk assessment
applications.justification: The model's use in providing more accurate GHG estimates plays a significant role in financial and risk assessments related to climate change.
applications.quote: These GHG emissions assessments measure exposure to transition risk and negative cash flows coming from fines or outflows to competitors with greener footprints.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper fits well within the existing categories related to Climate Change Mitigation and related sub-categories, specifically focusing on GHG measurement and tracking.
new_primary_category.quote: Our model is fully interpretable, the user being able to understand which factors explain the GHG emissions for each particular company.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The paper aligns with the existing sub-category of Greenhouse Gases Measurement and Tracking, and doesn't require a new sub-category.
